However, if this co-worker is clearly struggling and looks like they'd need help, I'd just approach them after the meeting is over after work and everyone has already left the room to ask them if they need help with anything. If they don't look like they're struggling that bad, I would probably just leave and not approach them at all.

question: If you notice a common friend consistently ignoring, marginalizing, or discriminatory acts towards a minority in your group, how do you intervene?
answer: I would intervene at the time they said something by pulling them up on it. Then they would not be able to deny it was something they ever did. I would emphasise it wasn’t something I wanted to hear again, then I would change the subject. This gives them the opportunity to change their behaviour without turning it into an argument immediately at the time.

question: If you notice a team member at work is consistently avoiding their responsibilities, how will you address it?
answer: I would hold a one to one intervention and communicate with them, evaluate their work ethic and responsibilities with them. Also reassess if this job role is suitable for them and would like to have other responsibilities more suited for them. Also see if they are doing well mentally.

question: If you overhear a personal conversation about a colleague at the workplace, how would you respond?
answer: I would probably ignore it. If the dialogue is not being directed at me then I have no right ot interfere in others business. If that conversation divulged information that I believe was illegal or predjudicial I may speak to my manager about the situation.

question: If you realized someone was significantly misinformed about a topic important to you, would you correct them? Why or why not?
answer: i probably would, depending on who they are and their relationship to me. The method off correction would depend on their status with respect to me. Are they a friend, are they a stranger, are they a superior? What would be the impact of correcting them to me or to them or both of us, Also I would need to consider how important it is to correct them. If life or limb is at steak and or an immediate concern then it becomes a higher priority and status can go by the wayside,

question: If you saw a friend being given preferential treatment due to their close relationship with the decision maker, how would you react?
answer: If I saw a friend being given preferential treatment due to their close relationship with the decision maker, I would be happy that my friend has such close connections. I would also be happy that they were my friend because, since they have such a close relationship with the decision maker, this could help me as well. It also gives me a connection to a decision maker and will perhaps help me be able to have a say in some things as well.

question: If you saw a stray animal on the side of the road, what would you do?
answer: I would be cautious as to ensure the animal was not with an owner and was a stray. I would gently go up to the animal and be sensitive and careful as not to scare it. I would check for any collars or chips which might tell me who or if it belongs to someone. If none of these were apparent, I would ring a close by vets and see if I could bring it in, but if it was late i would take it home and give it some food and drink and care for it until I could take it to a vets. I would also possibly post an image of the pet on social media to raise awareness and try to get it home.

question: If you saw someone accidentally drop their wallet, what would you do and why?
answer: I find this an easy question to answer as I was visiting a museum recently with my family and saw a tourist drop their hotel room card without realising and my response was exactly the same as it would be if it had been a wallet. If I noticed a stranger drop their wallet I would immediately catch their attention by loudly saying “excuse me” and at the same time I would move to retrieve the wallet from the ground before someone else would grab it. If they didn’t hear me by the time I had the wallet in my hand I would say it louder whilst at the same time holding out the wallet so they could see it as soon as they tuned around and know that I had a valid reason to be grabbing their attention. My reason for behaving this way is that, if I was in the person’s shoes, I would hope that another stranger would help me in this way. Whether the wallet was empty or stuffed full of money, my response would be exactly the same as my reasons would be unchanged by this fact.

question: If you saw two friends arguing in a heated manner, how would you choose to intervene or not?
answer: Unless the two friends are arguing in a way that directly involves me, I would likely not get involved. For instance, my direct involvement may mean I was the subject of their argument, or if they were in close proximity to me especially in a public space where their behavior was being noticed. Otherwise, I think it is best to let others resolve their conflicts and to not deregulate oneself due to their anger. One exception may be if the argument is about a third party that is in immediate distress or if they are arguing about a situation where someone’s well-being is at stake. In that case, I would likely get involved to help expedite matters so that person can be helped.

question: If you see an opportunity to gain something at the expense of someone else, what factors would influence your decision to act or not to act?
answer: If I saw an opportunity to gain something at the expense of someone else, I would have to weigh up the value of the said thing to both myself and the other person. It may be that one of us really values the thing and the other does not, then this would ultimately affect how I would act in the given opportunity. I would take the gain if it was something of value to me and not to the other person and I would not take the gain if the thing in question was of no value to me, but was of value to the other person. The matter gets a lot more complicated when the thing to be gained is of value to both people. In general I would try and be kind and allow the other person to have the thing at my expense. Unfortunately, this is not always possible. For example, in a work context you often have to aim for the same goals against rather than with colleagues. In cases such as this, I would have no option but to try and gain something at the expense of others. However, in-so-doing, I would always try to minimise the expense to others wherever I could do so and would only take from them what I absolutely had to. I would also try and be supportive of them in other contexts wherever possible.

question: If you see someone behaving in a way that you don't understand, what would your first step be to understand their behavior?
answer: I would step back and take a 360-degree view of the situation. If I know the person I would think about how this action differs from the norm or how it is similar to how they have acted previously. And I may just ask the person about their behavior if I'm feeling bold.

question: If you sense tension or discomfort in a social setting, how do you address it? If you choose not to, why?
answer: I think it's best to address these matters head on - the earlier it's addressed and resolved the less discomfort it causes

question: If you suspect someone’s motives are different from what they are expressing, what steps do you take to equip yourself with more clarity?
answer: If someone's motives seem different than what they claim to be, then ask which motive will they derive the most benefits from. Think about their character. Do they seem to be honest, moral, etc.? Have you seen them lie or take advantage of others before? You have to compile all the data you have on this person and decide how likely they are to have ulterior motives. If you can't come to a conclusion, you can ask them about it. Sometimes they will expose their true motives unwittingly.

question: If you were asked to distribute a prize among a group of participants based on their performance, how would you do it, and why?
answer: I would form a rubric that was as objective as possible and rate them on that rubric. I when then show them their scores and divide the prize based on those scores to maintain transparency and give the participants a sense that the competition was fair. This takes a lot of the guesswork out of it and allows people to know why they got what they got.

question: If you were at a social event and wanted to leave but your friends wanted to stay, how would you manage the situation?
answer: I think if I was in this situation then I would probably leave by myself, either in a taxi or I would call a family member for a lift home. I don't like to stay out later than I want to as I get very irritable.

question: If you were given credit for a great idea at work, but it was actually a colleague's idea, what would you do?
answer: I would feel guilty immediately, I wouldn't want to take credit for the idea, and would inform my employer that it was actually the idea of a colleague. I wouldn't want to create a conflict in the workplace with my colleague nor give myself the ethnical guilt that would come with taking credit for something I didn't come up with. If I were to take credit, I would understand the repercussions it could have. My colleague wouldn't trust me in the future, that colleague could tell others about my actions, resulting in long term issues as others wouldn't have the same level of trust in me that they once had.

question: If you were given the opportunity, would you volunteer at an animal shelter?
answer: I would definitely consider volunteering at an animal shelter. Volunteering at an animal shelter is a wonderful way to make a positive impact on the lives of animals in need. It allows individuals to provide care, attention, and love to animals awaiting adoption, contributing to their well-being and increasing their chances of finding forever homes. Additionally, volunteering at an animal shelter is an opportunity to support a noble cause, promote animal welfare, and be part of a community that shares a deep compassion for animals. It's a fulfilling and rewarding way to give back to the community and make a difference in the lives of vulnerable animals.

question: If you were given too much change at a store, would you keep it or alert the cashier to the mistake?

question: If you were offered a promotion at the cost of your colleague being fired, how would you handle it?

question: If you were to live in a country with a culture drastically different from yours, how would you prepare yourself to integrate and coexist smoothly?

question: If you were to negotiate, how would you plan your approach considering the second parties interests and psychology?
answer: I think negotiation is all about compromise. No one wants to feel like they're 'losing' in a negotiation. Use this to work out what your priority is in the negotiation. Then engineer your approach so that you are ensuring that you get as much as you can that you actually value. There will be some points of the negotiation that mean little to you, so let the other person 'win' big when it comes to those points. You can then leverage this to get what you want.

question: If you witness a public event that might be dangerous or illegal, what would you do and why?

question: If you witnessed an act of social injustice, would you intervene, report, or ignore it? Could you please explain your reasoning?

question: If you're having a conversation with someone and they suddenly cross their arms, how do you interpret that body language and how does it affect your interaction with them?
answer: Crossing one's arms in a conversation can indicate defensiveness or discomfort. However, I would interpret it as a potential sign of their personal comfort preference and not let it bother me. I'd continue the interaction with empathy, ensuring a non-judgmental and respectful environment.

question: If your best friend was suddenly acting distant and withdrawn, what steps would you take to understand their feelings and perspectives?
answer: If my best friend started acting distant and withdrawn, the first step I would take is to approach them gently and express my concern. I would let them know that I am here for them and that if something is bothering them, they can talk to me about it without any judgment. I would listen attentively and allow them to express themselves freely, without interrupting or trying to offer immediate solutions. It's important to create a safe space where they feel comfortable opening up about their feelings and perspectives. I would also try to put myself in their shoes and empathize with what they might be going through. Understanding that everyone has their own struggles and experiences can help avoid making assumptions or jumping to conclusions about their behavior. Additionally, I would remind myself to be patient and not push them to talk if they are not ready. Sometimes people need time to process and sort out their emotions on their own before they can share them with others. Showing genuine support and offering my help, whether it's through simply being there to listen or assisting with finding professional help if needed, is essential. Sometimes, reaching out and offering a helping hand can make a significant difference in someone's life. Ultimately, the key is to approach the situation with kindness, compassion, and respect. Being understanding and non-judgmental allows for a deeper connection and may provide the necessary space for my best friend to open up and share their feelings and perspectives.

question: If your boss was being unfairly critical of a colleague behind their back, how would you handle it?
answer: I would politely ask them to properly justify the reasons for the criticism while making it clear that criticising in that way is non-productive and engenders a negative working environment. question: If your classmate is consistently skipping group meetings for a project, how would you approach understanding their situation without blaming them right away?

question: If your close friend lied to protect your feelings, how would you react?
answer: If someone lied to protect my feelings, I would try hard to stifle the immediate flinch of wanting to respond negatively that comes when feeling like you’ve been deceived. It’s hard for people to not react negatively to lies, whether they are white lies or not, because there seems to be an innate disposition in the human condition that feels we are always owed the truth when it comes to anything that impacts us in any way. If I could temper my reaction, I would try to ask for some time to thoroughly think about what they’ve told me so that I can understand their perspective and their motivations. This would allow me to figure out how much of the intention had any negativity behind it, and whether or not it’s enough to warrant a certain level of reaction. There are many situations where even if one was lied to, it’s not worth reacting too harshly to, as the damage that reaction could cause may be more than what the initial lie may have done.

question: If your close friend unintentionally wrongs you, would you consider it less unfair than if a stranger did the same thing? Why or why not?

question: Imagine a scenario where a friend tells you a secret that could potentially hurt someone else. How would you navigate this situation?

question: Imagine that you are in a busy café, waiting in line to order your coffee. Suddenly, the person in front of you receives a phone call and answers it, leaving their spot unoccupied. How would you react? Would your response differ if the person seemed preoccupied or upset during the call?

question: Imagine there's a person who is avoiding social gatherings lately which is unusual for them? How would you find out what's wrong and what could be the possible reasons behind their changed behavior?

question: Imagine you are at a dinner party and you notice two guests are engaged in a heated argument. How would you handle the situation to maintain a peaceful atmosphere?

question: Imagine you’re in a group discussion where one person is being shy or quiet. What do you believe might be the thought process of this quiet person and how would you help them feel more comfortable?

question: In a professional setting, how do you deal with differing viewpoints when working towards a common goal?

question: In past disagreements with a close relationship, what strategies worked best to resolve the issue?

question: In queuing situations (food courts, hospital waiting rooms, etc.), how do you define fairness when giving turns? How would you react if someone does not respecting these norms?
answer: In queuing situations, I believe fairness in giving turns means treating everyone in the line with equal respect and consideration, regardless of their background or circumstances. It involves understanding that everyone's time is valuable and that we all deserve a fair chance to be served or attended to in an orderly manner. If someone does not respect these queuing norms, my reaction would depend on the situation and the severity of the violation. In most cases, I would try to approach the situation calmly and respectfully. I might politely inform the person about the queuing system and request that they join the line like everyone else. It's important to approach these situations with empathy, as it's possible that the person may not be aware of the established norms or might be going through a difficult situation that affects their behavior. However, if the violation continues or if it causes significant inconvenience to others, it may be appropriate to involve someone in authority, such as a staff member or security personnel, who can help address the issue. The key is to maintain composure and resolve conflicts in a manner that promotes understanding and fairness for all involved.

question: In relationships, how do you acknowledge your selfish tendencies, if any, and make sure they don't impede on the other person's happiness?

question: In settling misunderstandings, how do you ensure everyone has the opportunity for whose voice gets heard?

question: In the process of building trust, have instances of certain behaviors or actions led you to a path of distrust?

question: In what situation would you be kind to someone even when they may have wronged you?
answer: I believe in being kind to someone even when they may have wronged me, because kindness has the power to transcend personal grievances and promote understanding and growth. There are various situations in which I would choose kindness over retaliation or resentment. Firstly, I would choose kindness when I recognize that the individual may be facing personal challenges or going through a difficult time. Perhaps their actions were a result of stress, fear, or confusion. By responding with empathy and kindness, I can create an opportunity for them to feel supported, understood, and potentially reflect on their behavior. Secondly, I would prioritize kindness when I understand that holding onto anger or seeking revenge only perpetuates negativity. Choosing kindness instead allows for healing and promotes a positive atmosphere. It sends a message that I am willing to move past the wrong and cultivate a healthy relationship based on understanding and forgiveness. Additionally, kindness can be an effective tool for conflict resolution. By approaching the situation with empathy and open-mindedness, I can actively listen to the other person's perspective and find common ground. This approach can foster constructive dialogue, leading to a resolution that benefits both parties. Lastly, I would consider being kind even when someone wrongs me because I believe in the power of personal growth. Kindness does not mean forgetting or excusing the wrong, but it can create an opportunity for growth and change. Through compassion and forgiveness, there is a chance for the person to reflect on their actions, learn from their mistakes, and potentially make amends. In situations where someone has wronged me, choosing kindness might not be easy, but it embodies the qualities I aspire to have - understanding, compassion, and a belief in the potential for redemption. Ultimately, I strive to approach such situations with a mindset that allows for forgiveness, growth, and the possibility of rebuilding trust.

question: In what ways do you apply your values when you're in a leadership role or a team?
answer: When I am in a leadership role or part of a team, I strive to apply my values in various ways. I believe that showing empathy, understanding, and support can have a profound impact on the wellbeing and motivation of the individuals I lead or collaborate with. By fostering a positive and caring environment, I aim to empower others, boost morale, and create a sense of belonging. Overall, applying my values in a leadership role or within a team involves creating an inclusive, respectful, and empathetic environment, leading by example, promoting diversity, and showing kindness and compassion. These principles serve as a foundation for effective collaboration, personal growth, and achieving shared goals.

question: In what ways do you balance being authentic with being polite in social interactions?
answer: Authenticity does not mean being brutally honest and forthright about everything but rather showing that you have a personality that is not fake or deceitful but rather respectful and real. One may withhold negative comments to be polite but lying for personal gain is discouraged.

question: In what ways do you communicate empathy in a conversation or social interaction?
answer: In conversations or social interactions, communicating empathy often involves a blend of verbal and non-verbal cues. Active listening is foundational; by giving someone my full attention, I'm signalling that their thoughts and feelings matter. This creates a space for honest dialogue. Reflective statements can validate someone's experience. Repeating back what someone has said, in essence, shows that I'm engaged and trying to understand. This is particularly useful when discussing sensitive topics, as it demonstrates respect for what's being shared. Open body language, like maintaining eye contact and keeping an open posture, can make the interaction feel more inclusive. It's a non-verbal way to say, "I'm present and with you in this moment." Validating someone's emotions without judgment is another empathetic act. Using phrases like "That must be tough for you" can be more inclusive and respectful than saying something like "I know how you feel," which might unintentionally minimize their unique experience. Asking open-ended questions invites the other person to share more, allowing for a richer, more nuanced conversation. This is especially useful when discussing complex or sensitive topics, as it allows for a diversity of experiences and viewpoints to be expressed. Avoiding unsolicited advice is also key. People often just want to be heard, and offering solutions can sometimes come off as dismissive or insensitive, particularly when the topic is sensitive. The tone of voice is another crucial element. A warm, gentle tone can make the conversation feel inviting and respectful, encouraging the other person to open up more. Lastly, being mindful of cultural and social norms is important, as different cultures have their own ways of expressing and receiving empathy. Being aware of these differences can help make empathetic responses more universally understood and appreciated. Overall, the aim is to make the other person feel heard, respected, and valued, taking into account both what is said and how it is said.

question: In what ways do you convey respect for diverse viewpoints in a conversation or a discussion?
answer: As my previous response, interacting with people from diverse cultures, backgrounds, and viewpoints (among many others things) generally offers unique insights that can last a lifetime. Learning how others view the world, approach problems, and celebrate friendship, love, or business dealings can inspire and contribute to a better overall understanding of the big picture. It seems obvious to me, but for as many differences as there are between any two given people, our shared identity as humans living on one planet is the ultimate common denominator. I believe it’s for everyone’s best interest that we appreciate and foster better understanding of our individuality and diversity as a part of the complex nature of who we are. I try to represent myself well and display enough pride in the aspects of my makeup that contribute to who I am while remaining open to new ideas, values, etc as a continual, never-finished ‘work-in-progress’, and I believe that showcasing how I represent myself and value others should foster the same sense in a reciprocal sense. In other words, respect and value others and yourself, be open to new ideas or experiences, and never stop growing!

question: In what ways do you express empathy to ensure others feel seen and validated in their emotions?
answer: I express empathy to ensure others feel validated in their emotions in the following ways: I listen attentively. When someone is sharing their feelings with me, I give them my full attention. I validate their feelings. I let the person know that their feelings are valid and understandable. I offer support. I let the person know that I am there for them and that I want to help. It is important to be genuine when expressing empathy. People can tell when you are not being sincere.

question: In what ways do you foster a sense of social responsibility in the younger generation?
answer: Fostering a sense of social responsibility in the younger generation is vital for building a more compassionate and socially conscious society. This can be achieved by integrating social issues into education, introducing positive role models, promoting community involvement and volunteerism, emphasizing empathy, encouraging critical media consumption, instilling values and ethics, and empowering youth-led initiatives. By creating a supportive environment that values social responsibility, we can help young people become more engaged, and empathetic that prepares them to tackle complex challenges that come up.

question: In what ways do you interpret and respond to the tone of speech in various social situations?
answer: Listen to them closely.

question: In what ways do your ethical standards impact the way you conduct yourself in group settings?
answer: Ethical standards, if held closely, inform and impact every action we take in life. Take, for instance, a conversation where a crude joke or two is being shared. If I value my ethical standards related to respecting women, I would either not participate in that conversation at all, or I would speak up and say that I didn't think it was appropriate to discuss those things. Being ethical does not necessarily have to be a conscious choice, if you've grown accustomed to making the right choices anyway.

question: In what ways have you promoted inclusivity and diversity in your societal relationships?
answer: In my societal relationships, I have made a conscious effort to promote inclusivity and diversity by embracing different perspectives, experiences, and backgrounds. I actively listen to others without judgment and seek to understand their unique stories and struggles. I strive to create an environment where everyone feels respected, valued, and empowered to express themselves. I encourage open discussions about diversity and inclusion, allowing for all voices to be heard and understood. This means ensuring that people from various ethnicities, genders, sexual orientations, abilities, and backgrounds are represented and given an equal opportunity to participate. I also actively educate myself about different cultures, histories, and social issues, recognizing that inclusivity goes beyond just tolerating differences. By educating myself, I can challenge my own biases and foster greater empathy and understanding towards others. In my relationships, I actively advocate for equal opportunities and fair treatment, working towards dismantling systems of privilege and discrimination. I call out any acts of injustice or exclusion that I witness, whether big or small, and work towards creating an environment where everyone feels safe and supported. Overall, I believe that promoting inclusivity and diversity begins with the mindset of respect, empathy, and the commitment to actively challenge and change the norms that perpetuate exclusion. Through ongoing reflection and action, I strive to create a society where everyone can thrive and feel a sense of belonging.

question: In which situations do you find it hardest to take on someone else's perspective? Why?
answer: In challenging scenarios, taking on another's perspective can be tough due to deep-seated beliefs, emotional biases, limited information, and cultural differences. Stress and personality clashes also hinder empathy. Self-awareness and open dialogue are essential for overcoming these hurdles and fostering better understanding.

question: In your experience, can you share an instance where observing body language gave you a better understanding of the situation than the spoken words?
answer: Yes, I would be happy to share an instance where observing body language provided me with a better understanding of a situation than the spoken words. There was a time when I was working with a colleague who seemed to always be cheerful and enthusiastic during team meetings. However, during one particular meeting, their body language told a completely different story. They appeared tense, avoided eye contact, and their arms were crossed tightly across their chest. Intrigued by this contradiction, I decided to approach them after the meeting to check in and see if anything was on their mind. As we began discussing their feelings, they slowly opened up and shared that they had been struggling with a personal issue that was affecting their performance at work. They explained that they didn't want to burden anyone with their problems and felt it necessary to put on a positive front during the meetings. However, their body language revealed their true emotional state, which contradicted their spoken words. By acknowledging their body language and providing a safe and supportive space for them to express themselves, I was able to gain a deeper understanding of their situation. This allowed me to offer my support and resources, enabling them to address their personal issue and find a way to manage it without compromising their work. This experience highlighted the importance of paying attention to nonverbal cues, such as body language, which can often convey emotions and thoughts that spoken words may not express. It taught me to be more empathetic and understanding, as individuals may not always feel comfortable verbalizing their struggles. By actively observing body language, I can better understand people's emotions, needs, and perspectives, ultimately fostering more meaningful and supportive interpersonal relationships.

question: In your experience, how does understanding someone's values impact your relationship with them?
answer: Taking time to investigate someone's values can help increase the understanding between two people. In situations where the values of two people align or complement each other, understanding these similarities can make a relationship deeper, more authentic and more meaningful because you are exploring the inner life of another person, which may be greatly different to their outer persona, depending on the person. However, in some cases learning the values of another person can be a fractious decision, because you may learn that their values do not align enough with yours for a closer relationship. In these cases the impact might be very negative on the relationship. In others it may still increase the understanding of the person, which can make it easier to interact with that person regardless of whether you want to deepen the relationship or keep it casual. Overall, learning someone's values can be a very important tool to help you evaluate and make a decision about what kind of relationship you would like with a person. Greater understanding of others can enhance your empathy regardless, which is useful in interpersonal relationships.

question: In your experience, how has being socially responsible benefited you in your interpersonal relationships?
answer: Practicing social responsibility has had a positive impact on my personal relationships by fostering trust, respect, and dependability, while also enhancing my ability to communicate effectively and connect with others through improved empathy skills

question: In your opinion, are there certain actions or behaviors that are unforgivable and would result in permanent loss of trust?
answer: In my opinion, there are indeed actions or behaviors that can be considered unforgivable and may lead to a permanent loss of trust. These typically involve severe betrayals of trust, such as dishonesty, betrayal, or harm caused intentionally. The threshold for what is unforgivable can vary from person to person and situation to situation, but actions that fundamentally breach the core values or principles of a relationship often lead to a permanent erosion of trust.

question: In your opinion, are there situations where distrust is necessary for self-protection? Can you give examples?
answer: I think distrust can be necessary for self-protection in certain situations, and while generally I think a society needs to operate on trust, it should never be given blindly. A few examples that come to mind are social media and online interactions in general -- due to anonymity and the near impossibility of proving the identities of anyone in particular, I think one needs to have a baseline level of distrust or at least caution when dealing with others in an online space. Financial transactions with people or institutions is another -- one can never be too careful with one's money in this day and age, and there are scams everywhere, especially online. It is becoming more and more difficult to protect sensitive information in the digital age, so distrust is almost mandatory in many instances.

question: In your opinion, how important is it to understand the personal values of those around you?
answer: It is indeed important to understand values of others around you, that is life.

question: In your opinion, how important is it to use someone's correct gender pronouns?
answer: It's very important to use someone's correct gender pronouns because their gender is an important part of their identity. It shows respect and inclusivity to use the pronouns that someone else prefers. We all want to experience empathy and inclusion and being respectful of gender differences is an important way to practice these ideals. Though using unfamiliar pronouns can be a challenge, one can also practice and learn how to use unfamiliar pronouns appropriately.

question: In your opinion, is it important to educate children on animal welfare and caring for pets? Why or why not?
answer: In my opinion, it is important to educate children on animal welfare and caring for pets. There are several reasons why this education is crucial. Firstly, teaching children about animal welfare instills a sense of empathy and compassion towards animals. By understanding the needs and emotions of animals, children can develop a deep respect for all living beings and learn to treat them with kindness and care. This empathy extends beyond pets and can contribute to a more compassionate society overall. Secondly, educating children on caring for pets helps them understand the responsibilities that come with owning a pet. Pets require proper nutrition, exercise, grooming, and veterinary care. Teaching children about these needs can help them develop a sense of responsibility, patience, and commitment. It also helps them understand that pets are not just objects, but living beings that rely on humans for their well-being.

question: In your opinion, is it important to spay/neuter pets? Why or why not?
answer: Pets are, while still being living things deserving of respect and a good life, a luxury item that nobody has any right to. As can be seen in many countries, and through no fault of their own, non neutered pets will instinctively breed as much and for as long as they can, massively increasing the population. Resulting in suffering for both people and animals, who could become feral, dangerous, or subjected to a life of suffering. Neutering pets also has a side benefit of reducing the amount of some reproductive and hormonal instances and enables pets to live a longer and happier life in many cases.

question: In your opinion, is it more important to be fair or kind? Can you think of a situation where you had to choose between the two?
answer: Fair and kind are both important attributes, the hierarchy between the two is dependent on the situation. I have a family member that I had recently given a second chance but he keeps doing things that steal from my peace. I had to make a choice between remaining kind to him and let him mess with my peace of mind or separate from him thus giving him the fair treatment that he deserves. In this situation I chose to be fair to the both of us and I created distance from this individual.

question: In your opinion, what are some key elements in building and maintaining healthy relationships?
answer: Some key elements to building and maintaining relationships are honesty, trust, communication, empathy, respect, boundaries, and support. I think all of those are important in healthy relationships. Communication is key. It's important to talk to others and be honest with them so you can learn to trust each other. It's important to show respect to others, and it helps if you have empathy, that way you can put yourself in their shoes to better understand them and what they may be going through. I think boundaries are paramount in relationships. Setting healthy boundaries is good for everyone and strengthens relationships and your own self-worth. And it's important to show support for others so they feel like you have their back no matter what.

question: In your opinion, what are the integral components that constitute an act of kindness?
answer: I would say a) It has to be considered a positive act by the recipient b) It has to be motivated primarily by the benefit of the recipient, not the benefit of the person doing the act. c) I think it has to incur some sort of cost on the provider, even if it is a disproportionately small one.

question: In your opinion, what are your responsibilities to your society at large, and how do you fulfill those roles?
answer: My responsibility to my society at large is to not be a drain on it or a negative influence upon it. If I can have a positive effect on the society, that is great. But most important is that I don’t bring down the society at all. To fulfill this role I don’t take more than I deserve. I work a job and pay my own way. I do my best to help others and to be kind to strangers. I stay away from getting in arguments with strangers. I try to treat others in society the way I would want to be treated.

question: In your opinion, what does it mean to truly empathize with another person?
answer: To truly empathize with another person means to deeply understand and share in their feelings, experiences, and perspectives. It requires stepping outside of our own frame of reference and genuinely putting ourselves in their shoes. It entails listening attentively to their thoughts and emotions without judgment or interruption, allowing their voice to be heard and validated. Empathy involves recognizing and acknowledging their pain, joy, struggles, or successes, and responding with compassion and support. It also involves being open to learning from their experiences, broadening our own understanding, and fostering a sense of connection and solidarity. Genuine empathy extends beyond sympathy or pity; it is about genuinely connecting with another person on a deeper emotional level and showing them that they are seen, heard, and valued as a unique individual.

question: In your opinion, what is the best way to teach children about animal kindness and respect?
answer: It starts with the adults setting a proper example. Teaching them from and early age and showing them the proper way to act around animals. Which ones that can be pet and which ones should be left alone is important.

question: In your opinion, what role does assertiveness and confidence play in successful negotiations?
answer: Absolutely, in successful negotiations, assertiveness and confidence are vital for clearly stating your position and standing your ground. However, the empathy you show towards the other party's and the recognition of shared goals is even more important. It's not just about winning; it's about finding solutions!

question: In your opinion, what role does humility play in navigating complex social situations?
answer: Humility plays an important role in complicated social situations. When one is humble, one listens more, apologizes when wrong, and shows respect to others. This behavior helps connect with people, solve problems, and also avoid potential conflicts.

question: In your opinion, what tactics or social strategies are effective for maintaining healthy and meaningful relationships with others?
answer: I find it's important to occasionally review relationships with all friends, family and colleagues. If you don't then its easy for a relationship to fade or sour due to a lack of action from one party. By occasionally taking the time to reflect on how each relationship is progressing you can identify how and whether it is still working for both parties, and whether any changes are desirable. I find the best method to maintain and build healthy relationships is to focus on communication, both of what's new from my end, and what's happening in the other persons life. It's so easy to allow a relationship to whither due to a lack of communication in everyone's very busy lives, and so taking the time to check back in with someone I haven't spoken to for a while is important to keep a relationship going.

question: In your opinion, when is it appropriate to walk away from a negotiation?
answer: When they are being aggressive and unwilling to genuinely negotiate. Also, If they are acting emotionally and are unwilling to compromise with you.

question: In your perspective, do ends justify means? Why or why not?
answer: This is not always the case. There are many ways to go about things to get the necessary outcome and some are not at all ethical. As long as the ends are achieved in a fair and reasonable manner that that is perfectly acceptable. Achieving something where you have disrespected or hurt another person is not acceptable in my opinion.

question: In your perspective, how has social media influenced our generation's perception on gender sexuality, orientation, and identity?
answer: Because people are more open

question: In your understanding, does everyone need to be treated the same way to ensure fairness? Why or why not?
answer: I believe fairness works both ways and should be regarded as equal and just ~ if one person does as much as I do for them and is consistent, I will do the same. Fairness has to be something that's reciprocated both ways. I aim to be fair and kind to everyone, but I believe if one person shows me more respect than someone who doesn't bother, I am more likely to use my time and respect on them. Fairness needs to be reciprocated both ways to be earned and deserved.

question: In your view, in a disagreement, when should one compromise, stand their ground, or distance themselves? Why?
answer: In my view, the decision to compromise, stand my ground, or distance myself in a disagreement depends on the situation and the nature of the disagreement. Here are some general guidelines: - Compromise: If the disagreement is minor or if I am dealing with someone who is important to me, it may be best to compromise. This means finding a solution that we both can agree on, even if it means giving up some of what I originally wanted. Compromise can help maintain relationships and prevent unnecessary conflicts. - Stand my ground: If the issue is important to me and I feel strongly about it, it may be necessary to stand my ground. This means holding firm to my position and not giving in to pressure or manipulation. It's important to be respectful and open-minded, but also assertive and clear about my needs and boundaries. - Distance myself: If the other person is being aggressive, disrespectful, or abusive, it may be necessary to distance myself. This means removing myself from the situation and possibly ending the relationship. It's important to prioritize my own safety and well-being in these situations. Ultimately, the decision to compromise, stand my ground, or distance myself depends on my values, goals, and priorities. It's important to be honest with oneself and communicate clearly with the other person in order to find a resolution that works for everyone involved.

question: In your view, what would the world look like if everyone practiced kindness all the time?
answer: If only this were the case. The world would be a much happier place and everyone would be in a better mood and feel less bitterness and resentfulness against others. We need more kindness and compassion in the world.

question: In your view, who is responsible for determining what is ethical and what is not?
answer: Ultimately, it's up to individuals to develop their own moral compass. I do think however, that people as a whole will need some guidance, especially in their formative years. Different cultures will form different ethical standards that will vary based on factors such as religion, history, and traditions. Those ethical standards will then be encouraged through laws, education, media, religion and by parents raising their children. While these institutions can help to determine what is ethical or not, it's important for individuals to look outside of their cultural upbringing and make their own decisions as well. For example, someone raised in a religious environment might be taught that homosexuality is immoral. It ultimately comes down to the individual to use critical thinking to determine whether, just because they've been told that that is the case, whether it's actually true. And whether or not it is fair to discriminate someone based on a cultural belief.

question: Is it a social responsibility to vote or to be politically aware? Why do you believe so?
answer: It is absolutely a social responsibility to be politically aware and to vote. I believe this is so because we are so privileged to live in a country where we are free and have the right to influence how our country is ran. It's a country for the people by the people, you need to know what is happening politically and go out and be the voice of change if one is needed. We are blessed to have influence in the way that we can shape the way our country is and who the leadership is.

question: Is it acceptable to steal food if your family is starving? Why or why not?
answer: It could be. If you've tried every other means to acquire food and failed, and someone in your family is going to die, and you're stealing it from a place that has an abundance of food -- in that case, you would have no choice. What is NOT acceptable is someone starving to death when there is sufficient food available for every one.

question: Is it fair that different people have different benefits and drawbacks in their life? Can you expand on why you think this?
answer: Yes, it is fair that different people have different benefits and drawbacks in their life. Here are a few reasons why this is considered fair: 1. Each person is born with their own set of strengths, weaknesses, talents, and challenges. 2. Fairness does not mean that everyone should have the same benefits and drawbacks, but rather equal opportunities to pursue their goals and aspirations. It acknowledges that circumstances and abilities vary among individuals. Providing equal opportunities for all, regardless of their starting point, promotes fairness within a society 3. The presence of benefits and drawbacks in our lives provides opportunities for personal growth and development. Challenges and setbacks can lead to resilience, adaptability, and the acquisition of new skills.

question: Is it more important for you to fit into a group or stay true to your personal values? Why?
answer: Though I highly value being a part of a group or groups, I believe it is more important to be true to yourself. I have to look at myself in the mirror every day and ask, "did I maintain my values or change to fit in?" For my own self-esteem and self-satisfaction, I need to be true to myself and the group has to accept me for who I am.

question: Is it possible for humor to have deeper implications? Are there hidden truths in your jokes or humor?
answer: absolutely. Humor has the remarkable ability to convey deeper implications and hidden truth. Behind the laughter, jokes and humor often carry layers of meaning, social commentaries and reflections on various aspect of life.

question: Is it wrong to put animals in zoos? Why or why not?
answer: I would say putting animals in zoos is always going to be a debatable topic given it is an ethical conundrum. Personally, I would prefer there not be zoos; given it's usually completely a monetary gain scenario. Sanctuaries, on the other hand, I feel more positively towards. If there was a debate between the two sides I can imagine there would be several reasoning's for both sides. The reasons for keeping animals in zoos would be some of the following; the conservation of animals, as zoos often play a role in keeping endangered species going while conducting research that benefits both a captured and wild population of animal. The animals that are currently in captivity are less likely to be lost to natures whims. I would then say education; zoos are an opportunity for children and adults alike to visit, and learn about animals, allowing them to express and understand an interest in wildlife and their conservation. Lastly, I would say, rescue opportunities; some zoos would have the opportunity and power to rehabilitate injured or orphaned animals that would not survive in the wild, providing them with the chance to live healthier lives. On the other side, not keeping animals in zoos has plenty of reasons, and this would include the following; the welfare of the animals in captivity; many animals would struggle from confinement and limited space. As best as zoos try to meet the needs and natural environment of animals, there will never be a perfect image of that animals natural living conditions. I would say, the loss of freedom for animals, where because zoos are structured and adapted to running for humanity, it means animals lose the ability to roam, to hunt and to enjoy their natural instincts. I would say the key issue here are the zoos themselves, and whether the standards are up to scratch across the board. If zoos ran more like sanctuaries, and kept animals safe, and people to a distance, they'd be far better received.

question: Is there a time you felt really betrayed by someone close to you? What did you do to handle that experience?
answer: Betrayal is something we've all faced. I've felt betrayed by a family member. I handled it by just not communicating with them anymore. I don't hate them but I don't want them to be a part of my life because I can't trust them. We've both moved on and have accepted it.

question: Is there any circumstance where you believe it's acceptable to break the law?
answer: In general, no. But in specific situations, e.g. life or death situations, it may be acceptable to break the law. Breaking the law should be a last resort. For example, if someone broke their leg, it is not acceptable to speed to the hospital. If someone has been stabbed, in my opinion it is acceptable to speed to the hospital if no ambulances are available.

question: Is there anyone in your life whom you respect deeply? What makes you respect that person?
answer: The person I respect most in life is my mother. I respect her above all others as she is the most kind and caring person that I know. I feel her understanding in her words, but most importantly, her actions. She emphasizes with people, and she takes action to show that she is genuine in her feelings. It was her job to be this caring person in life, but even if it weren't, she would still have been. These traits do not always come automatically to a person like myself, and I've structured my life and actions to be more akin to my mother in how I treat other people. Treat others as you wish to be treated, and for that I respect her.

question: Is trust more important to you than love in a relationship? Why or why not?
answer: I think it is. To be in a relationship, it first has to be built on trust. You can love someone but not trust them; you'll start doubting everything they do, and you won't believe them if they say they love you. Without trust, the security of exposing yourself without judgment or fear is gone. This will all lead to love being lost and the relationship failing.

question: Jane is on a diet but really wants dessert after dinner. Her husband Steve suggests they share dessert. Why does Steve offer to share dessert with Jane?
answer: Steve offers to share dessert with Jane because he wants to support her in her dieting goals while also acknowledging and validating her desire for something sweet after dinner. By suggesting they share dessert, Steve is showing his love and care for Jane by helping her find a middle ground between sticking to her diet and still enjoying something she desires. He understands that it can be challenging to resist temptations when trying to make lifestyle changes, and by proposing to share dessert, he is offering a solution that allows them to both enjoy a treat without completely derailing Jane's progress. Steve's suggestion demonstrates his willingness to compromise and his thoughtfulness towards Jane's feelings and goals. Additionally, by sharing the dessert, Steve is also creating a bonding moment where they can enjoy each other's company and indulge in a delightful treat together.

question: Let's say you overhear your friend Sarah talking to a mutual friend, expressing excitement about a surprise party they're planning for her. Sarah doesn't know that you overheard the conversation. How might you navigate this situation to ensure the surprise isn't ruined, while also maintaining your knowledge of the surprise?
answer: If I were in this situation, my first instinct would be to respect the effort and thoughtfulness that Sarah has put into planning the surprise party. I would understand that her excitement is a natural response, but I would also want to ensure that the surprise is not ruined for her. To navigate this situation, I would act as though I haven't overheard the conversation. I wouldn't bring up the surprise party or show any indication that I am aware of it. I would avoid making comments or asking questions that might hint towards the surprise, as it could unintentionally spoil the excitement for Sarah. Instead, I would focus on supporting Sarah and making her feel special in other ways without giving away any details about the surprise. For example, I might plan a separate outing or gesture to celebrate her, and in doing so, uphold the surprise element of the actual party. It's important to consider how Sarah might feel if she were to inadvertently discover that I overheard her conversation, and to prioritize her feelings and the integrity of the surprise. Overall, the key is to maintain a sense of discretion and respect for Sarah's excitement and the efforts put into planning the surprise party, while also keeping my knowledge of the surprise to myself.

question: Let's say you're caught in the middle of two people sharing different stories about the same incident and asking you to take sides. What would you do?
answer: It is important to stay impartial in these situations to remain peaceful and empathetic. There are always two sides to every story, and each person may genuinely recall the events differently. Both people may be wrong, one may be wrong, or they may both be right, but in different variances. I would say to them that clearly they have interperated the same situation differently and taking sides would be wrong unless i knew what had happened.

question: Let's say you're planning a surprise birthday party for a friend. How would you go about keeping it a secret and ensuring that the surprise is genuine without giving any hints unintentionally?
answer: To keep a surprise party secret, you have to keep everything mundane and run-of-the-mill. For example, if it's a friend you regularly have dinner with, but doesn't usually come to your home then invite them to a dinner. On the way, say you left your wallet at home and have to run back. That way it isn't suspicious or unusual for them to come to your home. Just make it seem like a typical day overall.

question: Let's say you've received a mysterious emotive text from an acquaintance. Can you discuss how you'd determine their emotional state from the given message?
answer: If I received an emotive text from an acquaintance, I would be able to tell their emotional state by how they have worded the text. For example, if they were being very angry with the message they were trying to put across, I could tell this if they had made lots of mistakes with the spelling or grammar or if autocorrect had replaced words with the wrong words which they didn’t pick up on. If it was clear they had sent the text without re-reading it, this would suggest to me that they had hurriedly typed it and sent it as they were in so much of an emotional state that they just wanted to get the message sent urgently.

question: Maria wants ice cream. She goes to the freezer but there is no ice cream left. How does Maria feel when she sees there is no ice cream? Why?
answer: Maria feels disappointed when she sees there is no ice cream in the freezer because she had a desire for ice cream, and when her expectation of finding it in the freezer is not met, it results in a feeling of unhappiness.

question: Maryland law mandates you to change lanes when there's a stopped police or emergency vehicle on the side of the road. You know this but your friends, who have moved from Florida(where this law does not exist), do not. They're disappointed when you mysteriously toggle into the next lane after seeing police. How would you explain this situation in retrospect?
answer: This could be simply explained by informing them of the law in this state that stipulates this is what is required. This would act as education in case they were ever in similar circumstances again. They could also educate you, that the state they are from does not have this law and therefore if you remembered then you would not need to do this if ever visiting. I am not sure why they would be disappointed by you moving into the next lane, if you do not cause an accident then surely the driving of the vehicle is left to the driver. If they were following in a car behind then this might require more of an explanation as they may have been confused by the lane change and panic to follow.

question: Narrate a past situation where you used non-verbal cues to navigate a social situation.
answer: A few years ago, in an airport lounge, I saw the footballer Roy Keane. I was with my young son, who wanted to get Keanes autograph. Roy, is not exactly famed for his warmth and I was very hesitant to approach him. I stood with my son looking over at him, Roy noticed us and made eye contact with me, I smiled and nodded at my son. Roy Keane looked at my son, then back and me and then nodded at us. I took this to mean that he was 'happy' for us to approach him. We got an autograph!

question: On a crowded subway, you see an elderly person balancing precariously while standing up. How would you react to the situation? How would you balance their need for a seat and the potential discomfort of asking another person to give up their seat?
answer: I would ask them if they would like to take a seat. I would recognize right away that they need the seat more than I do, and would want to offer it to them as it feels like the morally right thing to do. I'm able to hand standing, but at their age, they could potentially fall, and I wouldn't want the guilt of seeing them get hurt. Asking another of the potential discomfort wouldn't be an issue, as the morality of the situation would come into play. Those of us who are more youthful understand the ethics that come into play when helping the elderly. It's very much etiquette to allow the elderly to have a spot when none are available.

question: Picture this: You're at a restaurant with a friend who has a severe food allergy. The server accidentally brings them a dish that contains the allergen. How do you think your friend would react to this situation? How would you offer support and assist them in handling it?
answer: The friend who has the allergy would be responsive to the server and tell them. If not I would tell them for the friend. I think it is acceptable to do this as accidents like eating food you are allergic to are always imminent and need to be resolved. It could mean a matter of life or death in some cases. So telling the server would be fine, hopefully they would react in time and replace the meal.

question: Picture yourself being in a crowded place, like a train station or an airport. How would you navigate through the crowd while considering the needs and intentions of other people around you?
answer: I would be mindful of my surroundings and respectful of the others who are and move through the crowd as well and I would move as carefully and quickly as possible, realizing that we are all probably in a hurry to get where we are going especially since this can often be a very stressful situation for some people with missed planes/trains, rushing to get to your destination, etc.

question: Reflect on a time when you observed a stranger holding back tears in public. What emotions did you experience while witnessing this? How did you react, if at all, and what factors influenced your decision?
answer: Recently, after leaving work, I stopped at a gas station to get gas and a few other things before heading home. At the gas pump next to me, I could hear, but not see, what sounded like a woman sobbing. I'm usually a pretty soft-hearted person, so I hate to see other people be upset and, especially, to cry. So I immediately started to feel quite awful for them. Usually, I'm not one to say something in a situation like this, both due to my own introversion and fear of making it worse. But, this time, however, I was heartbroken by her sobbing, so I sheepishly asked if she was okay. This actually ended up resulting a nearly 15 minute long conversation that went fairly well. She thanked me for listening and told me I made her day, which made me feel good as well.

question: Relate an instance where you found your views at significant variation with a lot of people. How did you empathize or appreciate their point of view?
answer: During a meeting with members of my team in a previous job, I suggested an improvement to the way we were working which I felt would increase our efficiency, but was met with scepticism from the other 16 people present. I thought I was coming up with a good idea and was initially taken aback by their negative response, but then tried to place myself in their shoes and understand why they were responding the way they were. I considered whether my suggestion might sound a bit radical, especially as they were used to working in a certain way, and what other objections they may have. This led me to conclude that their concerns were valid and before the firm could implement the change I was proposing, needed to be properly addressed. By adopting an empathetic attitude and imagining how my idea must sound to other team members, I was able to appreciate where they were coming from, and not dismiss their objections out of hand.

question: Sally puts her toy in a box and leaves the room. While she is gone, John moves the toy from the box to a basket. When Sally returns, where will she look for her toy? Why?
answer: Sally would go back to the location where she left the toy and that is the box. It is the last place she had the toy.

question: Sandra finds a wallet on the ground with money and cards inside. What should Sandra do? Why?
answer: If Sandra finds a wallet on the ground with money and cards inside, here are some things she could do: Look for identification: Check the wallet for any identification that could help locate the owner, such as a driver's license or business card. Contact the owner's bank or credit card company: If there are any cards in the wallet, Sandra could contact the bank or credit card company to report the lost wallet and provide the name or account number. They can then contact the owner and arrange for the wallet to be returned. Turn it in to the nearest police station: Sandra could turn the wallet in to the nearest police station, where it can be held until the owner comes to claim it.

question: Share a situation from your past where your empathy played a critical role.
answer: I was driving on a busy road in my town when I saw a small dog run into the road and the car in front of me struck it. The owner was in front of his house and distraught. The driver stopped and called the police, I stopped and got out and went to the owner because he seemed so sad and I felt so bad about it, even though it wasn't my fault I was just a witness. I stayed just to sit with him and make sure he was okay. I didn't know him at all. I don't know how critical it was but I like to think that this person today has a memory of some stranger being there for him during a difficult time and I like to think that mattered.

question: Share an occasion when you could pick up hints about someone’s unfamiliarity with a topic during a conversation. What signals precipitated your detection?
answer: One time, during a conversation about space exploration, I noticed someone's unfamiliarity with the topic. Some signals that helped me detect this included: Limited vocabulary: They struggled to use the right words and terms related to space, often using general or incorrect words. Lack of specific details: When discussing space missions or celestial bodies, they couldn't provide specific information and seemed unsure about the details. Questions indicating lack of knowledge: They asked basic questions about space, showing they didn't have much prior knowledge. Avoiding in-depth discussion: They tended to steer the conversation away from the topic, perhaps because they felt uncomfortable discussing it. These signals helped me realize that the person was not very familiar with the topic of space exploration.

question: Should fairness always be sought, even if it leads to conflicts or discomfort?
answer: Fairness in this context is a difficult subject to approach. When you see a disparity between individuals it can be difficult to not want to equalize the conditions between them, but what do you when "equalizing" involves taking away from the haves to give to the have-nots? Do you try to come up with some sort of justification to take away resources from another even if they earned those resources fairly or do you just turn a blind eye and try to accept that unfairness is an inherent part of life? Personally I don't believe in building up one person by tearing down another. Going forward we might have programs and other resources to help equalize conditions where those who need the most get the most and those who are not in need receive nothing and likely have the option to willingly contribute their own resources. I think the best we can do is try to slowly raise the floor in a way that is of benefit to everyone and in the mean time just accept that some disparity is just how it is. In short I do believe fairness should be sought but not in such a way that leads to large conflict or mass discomfort, especially if such discomfort involves unjustly taking from others (regardless of "justification" used) or it used as an act of vengeance to try and payback for past sins perpetrated by those who may not even be still around.

question: Should severe punishments be imposed on individuals found guilty of animal cruelty? How severe should these punishments be?
answer: Yes i believe it should be a 1 year or two year minimum prison sentence as animals can't defend themselves against humans

question: Should there be a time when being honest should outweigh the fear of being offensive? Explain why.
answer: I believe in most situations where no one's life is at risk, honesty should always be the leading commitment. I understand the anxiety that can come with being honest, but it should always be our primary goal.

question: Suppose a work colleague consistently submits reports late. How would you moderate your approach to this colleague? Can you speculate on the possible reasons for their tardiness?
answer: I would proabably speak to the collegaue to see if there was any support I could offer in any way, be that with work or personal situation. But I would not ush the point, I would just make myself avaliable to help if they required it. I would not be able to speculate on the reasons without more information.

question: Suppose someone behaves oddly during a conversation; according to you, what are the various factors you might consider before reacting to it and why?
answer: First, I would consider that they may not be feeling well so I would observe their behavior before speaking and if they continued to behave strangely, then I would politely ask them if they are ok or simply let them know that I don't understand the meaning of what they just did and ask them to explain it to me.

question: Suppose you find yourself in a situation where someone is repeatedly interrupting or talking over you during conversations. How would you address this issue assertively while maintaining a respectful and constructive dialogue?
answer: I would wait for a pause in the conversation or an opportunity to speak without interrupting. I would then acknowledge what the other person has said to demonstrate that I value their perspective. but I would be firm in stating my need to finish my thought or share my perspective.

question: Suppose you had to decide the distribution of bonuses in a team where everyone contributed fairly. However, one or two members took on significant tasks or project leading roles. Would you distribute evenly or proportionately? Why?
answer: I think in that situation i would distribute the bonuses evenly, as everyone had contributed to the task. If the one or two members continued to go above and beyond with future tasks, I would certainly look to reward them additionally moving forwards - perhaps has an additional end of year bonus for their extra help throughout the year.

question: Suppose your child has been acting out at school. How would you try to understand their perspective in order to address the situation?
answer: I would want to find out why they have been acting out, but not be hasty in trying to find out. I would let them know that I am there to talk with them and not be judgmental about what they have to say. I want them to feel comfortable and open up to me in how and why their acting out in school. I feel that be letting them know I am there to talk anytime they need me, they will eventually come to me and know they can discuss the issue with me without them feeing judged in return.

question: Taking care of a pet is a responsibility that demands time and resources, how do you manage it alongside other commitments like work, family and friends?
answer: I think it's important to identify your pet's needs and prioritise them alongside your own commitments ensuring you allocate enough time and resources for them. Establishing a consistent daily routine for feeding, exercise and playtime with your pet helps to create predictability for both you and your pet. It's also important to share responsibilities with family members or housemates and dividing the tasks such as feeding, grooming and walking between everyone, this allows you to commit to other stuff. Lastly, technology can also help for example automatic feeders or pet monitoring devices, or hiring a pet sitter which I personally can't afford but it's a viable option.

question: Tell about a time when you advised someone to change an unhealthy social behavior. What was the outcome?
answer: I had a friend named Sarah who had a chronic habit of always saying "yes" to every request or favor, regardless of her own well-being or comfort. She would often overextend herself, taking on more tasks and commitments than she could reasonably handle. This behavior left her feeling stressed, exhausted, and frequently unable to meet her own needs. One day, after noticing the toll this people-pleasing behavior was taking on her, I decided to have a candid conversation with Sarah. I approached it with sensitivity, expressing my concern for her well-being. I let her know that while her kindness and willingness to help others were admirable traits, it shouldn't come at the expense of her own happiness and mental health. During our conversation, I emphasized the importance of setting boundaries and learning to say "no" when necessary. I shared my own experiences and how I had learned the value of balance in my life. I explained that people who genuinely cared about her well-being would understand and respect her need to prioritize self-care. Initially, Sarah was apprehensive about the idea of changing her people-pleasing habits. She had grown accustomed to feeling responsible for meeting everyone's expectations and feared disappointing others. However, as we continued our discussions and I provided emotional support, she began to see the toll her behavior was taking on her own mental and physical health. Over time, Sarah started practicing setting boundaries and saying "no" when she felt overwhelmed or when a request didn't align with her priorities. It was challenging for her, and she faced some resistance and disappointment from certain individuals. However, she also found that many people respected her honesty and admired her commitment to self-care. The outcome of this situation was positive. Sarah's mental and physical health improved as she learned to prioritize her well-being. She experienced less stress and exhaustion and began to appreciate the freedom that came with setting boundaries. Our friendship remained strong throughout this process, and I was proud to see her gain confidence in her ability to make choices that were in her best interest.

question: Tell about a time when you sympathized with a person who initially put you off, based on any negative reviews about them you heard indirectly.
answer: I remember a situation where I encountered someone who, based on negative reviews I heard indirectly, initially put me off. However, as I got to know them personally, my perspective completely shifted. It was during a group project at work, and this person had a reputation for being difficult to work with as they were often described as controlling and confrontational. At first, I admit that I approached the project with some apprehension, expecting conflict and tension. However, as we started working together, I noticed that this individual had a deep passion for the subject matter and a strong commitment to accomplishing our shared goals. They were incredibly dedicated and had a keen eye for detail, which ultimately benefited the project. As the days went by, I took the opportunity to have personal conversations with them during our breaks. I learned that they had experienced some significant challenges in their personal life recently, which had inevitably influenced their behavior at work. Gradually, I began to empathize with what they were going through and realized that their seemingly abrasive nature was merely a response to their circumstances. As our conversations deepened, we found common ground and shared our own personal struggles. It was through this vulnerability that we started to develop a mutual understanding and respect for one another. I realized that their assertiveness was actually a result of their determination to produce the best outcome, rather than an intention to undermine or overpower the rest of the team. By the end of the project, not only did I sympathize with this individual, but I also appreciated their unique perspective and strong work ethic. Our team ultimately delivered an outstanding result, and I attributed a significant portion of our success to their drive and attention to detail. This experience taught me the importance of not solely relying on others' negative reviews and judgment when forming my own opinions. It highlighted the power of empathy and understanding in discovering the true nature of an individual beyond initial impressions.

question: Tell about a time when you were able to sense a shift in the room’s energy during a social gathering. How did you respond to it?
answer: One time, i remember when everyone was talking about a subject matter, everyone was in agreement with each other. But then one person in the room spoke up saying that what we thought was right, was wrong. So then i questioned this person about it. Why did they think we were wrong? how did they come to that opinion? I learned a lot about the subject matter from this person and thought they had some good ideas, but i still didn't agree with them.

question: Tell me about a time when you recognized and acknowledged a shortcoming or a blind spot in yourself. How did you work towards addressing it?
answer: About a year or so ago I went to an art forum and posted some of my work. I deliberately asked for critiques, but given the quality of the art that was posted there, I thought I stood above the average poster. What followed were several people pointing out several flaws within my work, flaws that I was utterly blind to, and offering their advice on how to overcome them. Although I asked for this I was somewhat crushed by their comments and retreated from the forum for a bit. In the end however I was forced to take their criticism to heart and recognized that my own personal attachment to my works blinded me to their faults. It was an eye opening experience and I ultimately set forth to correct my mistakes and adopted a more in depth method manner of creation going forward. Although it took great effort I believe I was able to address the issues that my original works had and even sought to recreate my favorites with my new methods and techniques I had learned. Putting the old work beside the new filled me with pride at my marked improvement but also filled me with a bit of cringe as I questioned how was I so unable to see all the flaws before.
